as_told.title: Guidance Technologies closes and Northrop's electrogravitics paper

plain: After the financier Floyd Odlum backed the inventor Townsend Brown, who worked on moving craft with electric fields, Brown shut his company Guidance Technologies in the fall of 1967 with no explanation, saying he got no results, and just three months later Odlum's company Northrop wrote a 1968 paper saying it was investing in electro-aerodynamics, Michels says in two documentaries. In one he also brings in an Aviation Week report on the B-2 bomber, and he names the general Curtis LeMay and the businessman Bill Lear in the story. He tells it as a sign that the work did not fail but went into a secret aerospace programme.
